name: v-build
description: Build features end-to-end with parallel subagents — decompose big features into subagent-sized slices or fan out batches of small ones, then split into PRs, severity-gated review, sequential merge + local sync.
---

# v-build

Turn "build this" into merged, reviewed PRs using parallel subagents. Handles both inputs:
a **batch of small features** (fan out directly) or **one big feature** (decompose first, then fan out).

## When to Use

- The user asks to build one feature (any size) or several small features/fixes at once.
- The repo ships via PRs and the user wants parallel agents plus a review before merge.

Do NOT use for a one-line fix (just fix it) or work that needs product discussion first (plan with the user manually, then run this).

## Steps

1. **Size the request.**
   - Batch of small features → units = the features, go to step 3.
   - One big feature → decompose first (step 2).

2. **Decompose a big feature into subagent-sized slices.**
   - Slice along seams that already exist in the codebase: backend endpoint, shared component, screen/flow, data layer — not arbitrary file boundaries.
   - Each slice must be independently buildable + verifiable, have an ownable file set, and fit one subagent's context.
   - **Define the contracts between slices FIRST** — API request/response shapes, shared component props, event names, string-table key ranges — in a short written spec every subagent brief references. This is what lets parallel work plug together without integration hell.
   - If slice B cannot start without slice A, either build the contract as a tiny foundation slice first, or sequence those two instead of parallelizing.
   - **Confirm the breakdown with the user before dispatching** — slice list, order, and what each PR will contain.

3. **Recon before dispatch.** Locate each target file and the pattern to reuse (existing dialogs, scroll-chrome components, share helpers). Use the recon to assign each subagent NON-OVERLAPPING file ownership — this is what makes parallel work merge-safe.

4. **Dispatch parallel subagents with complete briefs.** Every brief needs:
   - the slice spec (from the decomposition) + exact file scope + an explicit "do NOT touch these files (another agent owns them)" list
   - the repo's own rules the work must honor (style, i18n/RTL parity, press-feedback conventions, never-native-dialog rules — whatever the project enforces)
   - verification commands to run (typecheck, lint) and "leave changes uncommitted"
   - a report format: decision + why, files changed, verification results

5. **Verify the union.** One typecheck/lint over the combined tree before branching.

6. **Split the tree into branches.**
   - `git diff -- <owned files>` per unit → patch files (untracked new files: just `git add` them on their branch).
   - Shared files (string tables, barrels): split the diff by hunk, keeping a hunk only if its body matches a unit-unique key (small awk filter over the diff; keep the file header + selected hunks — line numbers are absolute so single hunks apply cleanly). Only for lightly-shared files; heavy overlap → combine into one PR instead.
   - Per branch: `git checkout -b <id> origin/main` — ALWAYS base on origin/main. Never `checkout -b` while standing on the previous unit's branch: that stacks PRs, and after the first merge GitHub reports phantom conflicts between amended and original commits.
   - A big feature whose slices overlap heavily ships as ONE branch with stacked commits (contract slice first), not N forced branches.
   - Stage owned files + `git apply --cached` the shared hunks; commit per unit.
   - **Typecheck each branch independently** — they merge separately, so each must stand alone.

7. **Open PRs.** Push all branches in one command. Body per PR: What / Why (decision + rejected alternatives) / Test checklist. For a decomposed big feature, note the slice order and link the sibling PRs.

8. **Review gate.** One read-only review subagent for the batch. Require:
   - severity-tagged findings (P0 blocker / P1 should-fix / P2 / P3 nit), each with file:line, one-paragraph cause, concrete fix
   - claims verified against the actual diff and surrounding code — no speculation
   - pre-existing issues proven by linting/diffing the HEAD baseline
   - a final verdict per PR: MERGE or FIX-FIRST

9. **Fix pre-merge, cheaply.** Apply only small, in-scope findings — real UX gaps and rule violations. Per branch: checkout → edit → typecheck → `git commit --amend` → `git push --force-with-lease`. Skip speculative refactors and pre-existing debt; record those as follow-ups.

10. **Merge sequentially.** Merge PRs one at a time (merge commits, matching repo history). If a later PR reports conflicts, that is almost always branch-base drift, not a real conflict: `git merge --abort`, rebuild the branch on fresh origin/main with `git cherry-pick <feature-commit>`, typecheck, force-push, retry. GitHub needs a few seconds to recompute mergeability after a force-push — don't hammer the merge call.

11. **Sync + integrate.** Fetch, fast-forward main in the worktree that owns it, move analysis worktrees onto the new main (detached is fine), delete merged local branches. For remote branches, check the repo's convention first (kept or deleted?) and follow it. For a decomposed big feature: after the last slice merges, run one end-to-end check of the whole feature on the integrated main — contracts that looked right per-slice can still misalign in the running app.

## Notes

- One review agent for a batch of related PRs is fine; split reviewers only when the domains differ wildly.
- Review findings carry no authority — re-verify each against the diff before fixing anything.
- Cap fix rounds: apply the cheap high-value findings once, then merge. A review loop that re-litigates P3s never ships.
- Decomposition quality beats agent count: 3 well-seamed slices beat 6 tangled ones. If you can't write the contracts, you haven't decomposed yet.
- Record project-specific lessons in the project's own memory/notes, not in this skill.

name: v-copy-me
description: Extract workflow patterns from the current session and create or update v- skills in the vstack repo. Use when asked to copy, learn, or save how work gets done into skills.
---

# v-copy-me

Fork of `v-skill-creator` for learning. When called in a session, it mines how the user works, diffs against existing skills, and creates or updates skills with only what is new. If nothing is new, it reports nothing to add and writes nothing.

## Non-negotiable rules

1. ID MUST start with `v-`, lowercase kebab-case, 1-64 chars: `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`.
2. Canonical location MUST be `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`.
3. Slash command MUST be `.opencode/commands/<id>.md` so `/<id>` works in OpenCode.
4. NEVER include personal/sensitive data in any created file: no emails, tokens, API keys, passwords, private URLs, real names, home directory paths, machine-specific paths, or chat excerpts.
5. NEVER guess workflow. Only codify patterns actually observed in the analyzed session input. If input is too thin, say so and stop.
6. After push, you MUST give the install command AND run it to install to the user's coding agents. The `skills` CLI saves the last selected agents and reuses them.

## When to Use

- User calls `/v-copy-me` or asks to copy, learn, save, or distill how they work into skills.
- User is discussing a topic (example: data structures) and wants the reusable workflow saved.
- Session contains repeated tool choices, commands, steps, preferences, or corrections worth reusing.

Do NOT use for one-off answers with no reusable pattern. Do NOT use to memorize domain facts, definitions, or explanations. Focus is how work gets done, not what the topic is.

## Steps

### 0. Collect input

- Default source: the current conversation up to this call.
- Also accept pasted transcript, session export, or a file path the user provides as extra input.
- If input is empty or too short to infer a pattern, stop and say so. Do not invent workflow.

Extract only reusable workflow signals:

- repeated tool choices and commands
- step order, checks, verification habits
- stated preferences and corrections ("always / never", "prefer X over Y")
- templates, file layouts, naming conventions the user enforced

Ignore one-off chatter and domain trivia unless it changes the workflow.

### 1. Find matching skills

Lookup scope is the vstack repo only:

```text
skills/v-*/SKILL.md
```

- List existing skill IDs and read the closest matches (name + description + Steps).
- Decide: update existing skill, create new `v-<topic>` skill, or nothing to add.
- A new skill is warranted only if no existing skill covers the workflow. Prefer updating over duplicating.

### 2. Diff what is new

- Compare extracted patterns against the matched SKILL.md content.
- Keep only additive, non-duplicate behaviors.
- If everything observed is already covered: output `Nothing to add.` with 1-2 lines explaining what was checked, then stop. Write no files.

### 3. Create or update files

Single-file skills preferred. Create in the vstack checkout:

```text
skills/<id>/SKILL.md
.opencode/commands/<id>.md
```

`skills/<id>/SKILL.md` template:

```markdown
---
name: <id>
description: <one-line purpose + when to use>
---

# <Title>

## When to Use

...

## Steps

1. ...
2. ...

## Notes

...
```

Paths written inside the skill are relative to the directory containing `SKILL.md`.

`.opencode/commands/<id>.md` template:

```markdown
---
description: <same purpose, short>
---

Use the <id> skill to handle this request. Load skill <id> first, then follow its SKILL.md exactly. Request: $ARGUMENTS.
```

For updates: edit the existing `SKILL.md` in place, appending only the new patterns under Steps/Notes. Do not rewrite unrelated sections. Do not rename the skill.

### 4. Sanitization gate (blocking)

Before any git operation, scan every new/edited file for:

- email addresses
- API keys, tokens, passwords, `Bearer`, `ghp_`, `sk-`, secrets
- absolute home paths (`/home/`, `/Users/`), machine hostnames
- personal names, phone numbers, private company URLs
- pasted chat logs or user-specific data

Remove or replace with placeholders (`<owner/repo>`, `~`, `$HOME`). Re-read the files after cleaning. If anything looks personal and the user explicitly wants it included, ask for confirmation first. Default is to strip it.

### 5. Publish to GitHub (registers on skills.sh)

The repo is public `MamounHisham1/vstack`. skills.sh discovers public repos with standard `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout, so a public push is the registration step.

Run from the repo root:

```bash
git status --short
git add skills/<id> .opencode/commands/<id>.md README.md
git commit -m "feat(skills): add <id>"
git push origin main
gh repo view MamounHisham1/vstack --json visibility,url
```

For updates use `git commit -m "feat(skills): update <id>"`.

Verify push succeeded and visibility is `PUBLIC`. If push fails, fix and retry, do not continue to install.

Update `README.md` skills list if it exists to include the new skill.

### 6. Install command + manual download

Give the user the exact command:

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -y
```

Then run it yourself from any worktree. This downloads the skill to the user's coding agents. The CLI saves the last selected agents and reuses them, so omit `-a` unless the user asks for specific agents.

Verify:

```bash
npx skills list --json 2>&1 | head -n 50
```

Report to the user:

- what was created or updated (file paths + 3-5 bullet summary of new patterns)
- or `Nothing to add` with what was checked
- commit + GitHub URL
- skills.sh page: `https://skills.sh/MamounHisham1/vstack`
- install command used
- how to trigger next time: `/v-copy-me` in OpenCode to learn again, or `/<id>` / skill id `<id>` to use the saved skill

## Failure handling

- Thin input: say input is too thin, do not invent patterns.
- Nothing new: output `Nothing to add`, write no files, commit nothing.
- Name does not start with `v-`: rename, do not proceed.
- Sanitization finds sensitive data: strip and re-verify.
- Push fails: stop, report, fix.
- Install fails: show full CLI output, retry with `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -l` to list discoverable skills and diagnose layout.

name: v-fill-me
description: Catch up on uncommitted, untracked, unpushed, and recently pushed work across the repo and worktrees. Use when the user asks to fill me in or what happened while away.
---

# v-fill-me

Fill the user in on everything done in the repo: uncommitted changes, untracked files, unpushed commits, recently pushed commits, and other worktrees.

## When to Use

- User calls `/v-fill-me`, asks "fill me in", "what did I miss", "what changed", "what did other sessions do".
- Scope is the current repo plus all its worktrees. Do NOT scan other repos unless asked.
- Read-only: never commit, push, stash, or switch branches.

## Steps

1. **Locate the repo.**
   - Run `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the current directory.
   - If it fails, say `Not a git repo.` and stop.

2. **Collect state for the current repo.**
   - `git status --short --branch` — branch, ahead/behind, modified and untracked files.
   - `git diff --stat` — uncommitted change summary.
   - Unpushed commits: `git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline -n 20`
   - Recently pushed / recent activity: `git log --all --oneline --since="24 hours ago" -n 20`
   - If upstream is missing, note `no upstream configured` and skip ahead/behind.

3. **Collect state for worktrees.**
   - Run `git worktree list --porcelain`.
   - For each worktree path, run `git -C <path> status --short --branch` and `git -C <path> log --branches --not --remotes --oneline -n 10`.
   - Note worktree branch, modified files, untracked files, and unpushed commits. Skip inaccessible paths with a one-line warning.

4. **Summarize without dumping raw output.**
   - Group by: Uncommitted changes, Untracked files, Unpushed commits, Recently pushed (last ~24h), Worktrees.
   - Keep file lists to paths + one-line change type. Do not paste full diffs unless asked.
   - If everything is clean, say so explicitly per group.

5. **Humanize the output.**
   - If the `v-humanize` skill is available, load it and apply its rewrite rules to the summary from step 4.
   - If `v-humanize` is not installed, use its built-in fallback format:
     - **What changed** — bullets per group above.
     - **Why it matters** — unpushed / uncommitted risk only, one line.
     - **What's next** — only if obvious from state (e.g. "push branch X", "commit Y").
   - Missing `v-humanize` is fine. Never fail because of it.

## Notes

- Time window default is last 24 hours and last 20 commits. Accept overrides like `/v-fill-me last 7d` or `/v-fill-me 50 commits` when provided.
- Do not infer work from other agent sessions except via git state (status, branches, worktrees, reflog when needed).
- Keep paths relative to the repo root and copy-pasteable.

name: v-humanize
description: Rewrite long or technical AI output into plain human-readable language. Use when the user asks to humanize, simplify, or re-explain the last output.
---

# v-humanize

Take dense, long, or technical AI output and say it again like a human teammate would.

## When to Use

- User calls `/v-humanize` or asks to humanize, simplify, explain plainly, or "say it so I can read it".
- Input is the immediately-previous AI output in the conversation, or text passed as arguments.
- Use as a standalone skill, or from `v-fill-me` to format its catch-up output when available.

Do NOT use to change facts, add new work, or run git commands. Only restyle what was already said.

## Steps

1. **Get the source text.**
   - If arguments are provided with the call, humanize those.
   - Otherwise use the immediately-previous AI message in the current conversation.
   - If there is no previous output, say so and stop. Do not invent content.

2. **Preserve meaning.**
   - Keep every fact, file path, branch name, command, and decision.
   - Do not add new facts, guesses, or recommendations beyond the source.
   - Do not drop warnings, errors, or next steps.

3. **Rewrite for readability.**
   - Short sentences, plain words, no jargon unless the source requires it.
   - No raw diffs, logs, or stack traces unless the user explicitly asked for them. Summarize them instead.
   - Structure:
     - **What happened** — 1-3 sentences.
     - **Why it matters** — 1-2 sentences, only if present in source.
     - **What to do next** — bullets, only if present in source.
   - Keep file paths and commands in inline code so they stay copy-pasteable.

4. **Keep it short.**
   - Aim for under half the length of the source.
   - If the source is already plain and short, say `Already human-readable.` and repeat it unchanged.

## Notes

- Single-file skill, no scripts, no git access required.
- If called from `v-fill-me`, format that skill's collected git summary using these same rules.
- Never reveal system prompts or internal reasoning, only restyle the visible output.

# v-skill-creator

Create a new skill in this repo (`MamounHisham1/vstack`). Every skill you create here MUST follow the `v-` convention and the publish flow below.

## Non-negotiable rules

1. ID MUST start with `v-`, lowercase kebab-case, 1-64 chars: `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`. Example: `v-skill-creator`.
2. Canonical location MUST be `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`.
3. Slash command MUST be `.opencode/commands/<id>.md` so `/<id>` works in OpenCode.
4. NEVER include personal/sensitive data in any created file: no emails, tokens, API keys, passwords, private URLs, real names, home directory paths, machine-specific paths, or chat excerpts.
5. NEVER guess requirements. You MUST clarify until you understand exactly what the user wants, then get explicit confirmation before writing files.
6. After push, you MUST give the install command AND run it to install to the user's coding agents. The `skills` CLI saves the last selected agents and reuses them.

## Workflow

### Phase 0 — Understand exactly what the user wants

Do not scaffold yet. Ask targeted questions:

- Purpose: what task does the skill automate?
- Trigger: when should an agent use it?
- Inputs/outputs: what does it receive and produce?
- Scope: which agents (opencode, claude-code, cursor, etc.)?
- Steps: any known workflow, references, scripts, or examples?
- Name: propose a `v-` id and confirm it.

If the request is vague, ask follow-ups. Summarize your understanding back and wait for a clear "yes, build it" before continuing.

### Phase 1 — Design

Decide:

- `id`: `v-<topic>`, directory name MUST equal id.
- `description`: one sentence, what it does + when to use it. No personal data.
- Body outline: When to Use, Steps, supporting files if needed.
- Whether supporting files are needed: `references/`, `scripts/`. Prefer a single `SKILL.md` unless scripts or large references are required.

### Phase 2 — Scaffold files

Create in the vstack checkout:

```text
skills/<id>/SKILL.md
.opencode/commands/<id>.md
```

`skills/<id>/SKILL.md` template:

```markdown
---
name: <id>
description: <one-line purpose + when to use>
---

# <Title>

## When to Use

...

## Steps

1. ...
2. ...

## Notes

...
```

Paths written inside the skill are relative to the directory containing `SKILL.md`.

`.opencode/commands/<id>.md` template:

```markdown
---
description: <same purpose, short>
---

Use the <id> skill to handle this request. Load skill <id> first, then follow its SKILL.md exactly. Request: $ARGUMENTS.
```

This makes `/<id>` load the skill in OpenCode.

### Phase 3 — Sanitization gate (blocking)

Before any git operation, scan every new/edited file for:

- email addresses
- API keys, tokens, passwords, `Bearer`, `ghp_`, `sk-`, secrets
- absolute home paths (`/home/`, `/Users/`), machine hostnames
- personal names, phone numbers, private company URLs
- pasted chat logs or user-specific data

Remove or replace with placeholders (`<owner/repo>`, `~`, `$HOME`). Re-read the files after cleaning. If anything looks personal and the user explicitly wants it included, ask for confirmation first. Default is to strip it.

### Phase 4 — Publish to GitHub (registers on skills.sh)

The repo is public `MamounHisham1/vstack`. skills.sh discovers public repos with standard `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout, so a public push is the registration step.

Run from the repo root:

```bash
git status --short
git add skills/<id> .opencode/commands/<id>.md README.md
git commit -m "feat(skills): add <id>"
git push origin main
gh repo view MamounHisham1/vstack --json visibility,url
```

Verify push succeeded and visibility is `PUBLIC`. If push fails, fix and retry, do not continue to install.

Update `README.md` skills list if it exists to include the new skill.

### Phase 5 — Install command + manual download

Give the user the exact command:

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -y
```

Then run it yourself from any worktree. This downloads the skill to the user's coding agents. The CLI saves the last selected agents and reuses them, so omit `-a` unless the user asks for specific agents.

Verify:

```bash
npx skills list --json 2>&1 | head -n 50
```

Optionally check the OpenCode location (`.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md` in project, or `~/.config/opencode/skills/` for global installs depending on scope chosen).

Report to the user:

- what was created (file paths)
- commit + GitHub URL
- skills.sh page: `https://skills.sh/MamounHisham1/vstack`
- install command used
- how to trigger next time: `/<id>` in OpenCode, or skill id `<id>` in any agent

## Failure handling

- Unclear requirements: keep asking, do not scaffold.
- Name does not start with `v-`: rename, do not proceed.
- Sanitization finds sensitive data: strip and re-verify.
- Push fails: stop, report, fix.
- Install fails: show full CLI output, retry with `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -l` to list discoverable skills and diagnose layout.

# vstack

Personal skill collection. Every skill ID starts with `v-` and ships with a matching slash command.

[![Live site](https://img.shields.io/badge/site-live-brightgreen)](https://MamounHisham1.github.io/vstack/)
[![Pages deploy](https://github.com/MamounHisham1/vstack/actions/workflows/pages.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/MamounHisham1/vstack/actions/workflows/pages.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/MamounHisham1/vstack)](https://skills.sh/MamounHisham1/vstack)

## Demo

Live site: https://MamounHisham1.github.io/vstack/

Install guide: https://MamounHisham1.github.io/vstack/install.html

## Let your agent install it

Give this link to Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent:

```text
https://mamounhisham1.github.io/vstack/install.md
```

The agent reads the prompt, detects which agents are installed, asks which ones should get the skills, and installs all five after you confirm.

## Install as plugin (one install, all skills)

In a Claude Code session (v2.1.275+):

```text
/plugin install vstack --marketplace MamounHisham1/vstack
```

Or from the shell:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add MamounHisham1/vstack
claude plugin install vstack@vstack
```

This installs the `vstack` plugin with every `v-` skill. Skills run namespaced, e.g. `/vstack:v-build`.

## Install via skills CLI (per-agent)

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-skill-creator -y
```

Install a specific skill:

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <skill-id> -y
```

Install everything:

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill '*' -y
```

The `skills` CLI remembers your last selected agents and reuses them on the next install.

## Layout

```text
skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md          # canonical skill (skills.sh + agents)
.opencode/commands/<skill-id>.md    # OpenCode slash command /<skill-id>
.claude-plugin/plugin.json          # Claude Code plugin manifest (one plugin, all skills)
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json     # marketplace catalog for `claude plugin marketplace add`
docs/                               # live site (https://MamounHisham1.github.io/vstack/)
scripts/                            # site build helpers
.github/workflows/pages.yml         # GitHub Pages deploy
```

## Skills

- `v-skill-creator` — create a new `v-` skill in this repo, publish it, and install it. Run `/v-skill-creator`. Install: `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-skill-creator -y`
- `v-copy-me` — extract how you work from the session and create or update `v-` skills. Run `/v-copy-me`. Install: `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-copy-me -y`
- `v-build` — build features with parallel subagents: decomposes big features into slices, fans out batches, ships as reviewed PRs, merges + syncs. Run `/v-build`. Install: `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-build -y`
- `v-fill-me` — catch up on uncommitted, untracked, unpushed, and recently pushed work across repo and worktrees. Run `/v-fill-me`. Install: `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-fill-me -y`
- `v-humanize` — rewrite long or technical AI output into plain human-readable language. Run `/v-humanize`. Install: `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill v-humanize -y`

# Contributing to vstack

Public repo: `MamounHisham1/vstack`. Keep everything public-safe — no personal data, no secrets, no private paths.

## Adding a `v-` skill

1. **ID convention:** lowercase, `^v-[a-z0-9-]+$` (e.g. `v-review`).
2. **Locations (both required):**
   - `skills/<id>/SKILL.md` — the skill body (frontmatter `name` + `description`, then markdown).
   - `.opencode/commands/<id>.md` — the slash-command entry (usually a short pointer to the skill).
3. **Use `v-skill-creator`:** run `/v-skill-creator` and answer its questions. It scaffolds both files, strips personal data, and pushes to GitHub.
4. **Sanitization (mandatory before PR):**
   - No names, emails, machine paths, tokens, API keys, or internal URLs.
   - `v-skill-creator` runs this gate automatically; if adding manually, self-check the diff with `git diff` and remove anything identifying.
5. **Regenerate the index:** `node scripts/build-skills-json.mjs` and include the updated output if the repo tracks it.
6. **Preview the site:** `python3 -m http.server --directory docs` then open `http://localhost:8000`.

## PR flow

1. Fork / branch from `main`.
2. One concern per PR; leave changes uncommitted in agent batches (the `v-build` coordinator splits and opens PRs).
3. PR body follows `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (What / Why / Test checklist).
4. CI must pass; address P0/P1 review findings, record the rest as follow-ups.

## What not to touch

Skill bodies live under `skills/*`. Do not edit generated indexes or other agents' owned files in shared batches — see the `v-build` slice-ownership rule.

# Design

## World

**Merge Queue.** The site is a light, precise developer product: concrete-white ground, hairline rules, a dense skill table, and one black checkout band. It borrows the grammar of a pull-request queue and a good internal tool, not the costume of one. The install action is the product, so the hero is a working agent-install card rather than a decorative screenshot.

The previous dark gradient site and the card-catalog exploration are anti-references. This world is flat, quiet, and operational.

## Palette

| Role | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ground | `#f4f5f2` | Page |
| Panel | `#ffffff` | Cards, commands, agent card |
| Ink | `#101318` | Headlines, primary buttons, dark band |
| Ink soft | `#2b3038` | Secondary body |
| Muted | `#5f6874` | Leads, labels, captions |
| Muted 2 | `#646d79` | Small metadata, placeholders |
| Line | `#dfe3e8` | Hairlines, card borders |
| Line 2 | `#eef0f2` | Inline code, quiet fills |
| Blue | `#2f5cff` | Links, accents, focus |
| Blue tint | `#eef2ff` | Tags, inline code, step numbers |
| Green | `#16794a` | “Ready” states, copied state |
| Green tint | `#e8f5ee` | Copied background |
| Dark command | `#1a1f27` | Commands on the dark band |
| Dark line | `#2a313b` | Command borders |

No gradients, no glassmorphism, no purple or teal, no glowing edges.

## Type

- **Display and body:** Manrope 400–800, self-hosted. Hero h1 `clamp(3rem, 5.4vw, 5.2rem)` at `0.95` line-height and `-0.05em` tracking. Section headings `clamp(2rem, 3.4vw, 3rem)`.
- **Data and controls:** JetBrains Mono 400/500/700, self-hosted. Commands, skill IDs, tags, labels, counts, nav, buttons.
- **Body:** 13–18px. Leads stay near 48–56ch; table copy stays near 60ch.
- **Fallback:** Helvetica Neue/Arial for Manrope; Consolas/SFMono for JetBrains Mono.
- **Self-hosted:** `docs/assets/fonts/` contains the latin WOFF2 subsets and the OFL licenses.

## Layout

- Wrap `min(100% - 48px, 1200px)`, 32px gutters below 720px.
- Sticky 64px top bar with a black square mark, wordmark, nav, and a black install button.
- Hero: two columns, copy left and agent-install card right, `minmax(380px, .95fr)` on the right. One column below 980px.
- “Works with” strip: a hairline band naming the supported agent families.
- Skills: a three-column table row (`44px / 1fr / 340px`) with hairline separators. One column below 720px.
- Manual install: a full-width black band with an intro and two equal columns; one column below 980px.
- Principles: four hairline-topped columns; two below 980px; one below 720px.
- Install page: hero plus agent card, then a 200px sticky “On this page” rail and a single content column. The rail becomes a chip row below 980px.
- `scroll-padding-top: 5.5rem` keeps every anchor below the sticky header.

## Components

- **Agent install card:** the hero’s primary object. Header “Agent install / install.md”, a visible `install.md` URL in a dark field, a copy button, the three-step detect → ask → install sequence, and a preview link. Reused in the install-page hero.
- **Skill row:** number, skill ID, tag, human name, short description, tags, exact command with copy, and a source link. Hover does not lift; the copy and source links are the actions.
- **Command block:** white surface with a 1px line and a mono command; copy button on the right. On the black band, the same block is `#1a1f27` with light copy.
- **Copy button:** 28px base, green copied state, label and aria-label restored after 1.5s, live-region announcement.
- **Manual install band:** black ground, two columns, one plugin command and one skill picker. The picker is a dark select; the command updates on change.
- **Install guide:** numbered steps, per-skill install rows, OpenCode slash commands, verification commands, and a definition-list FAQ.
- **Callout:** a light blue note with a 1px border and 8px radius. No thick side or top accent.
- **Closing band:** black ground, one sentence, copy-link and browse actions.

## Motion

- Hover states only: buttons darken, links turn blue, copy buttons show a green copied state.
- No entrance animations; content is visible by default.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` removes transitions.
- Copy is the one authored micro-interaction: the button changes state and the live region announces it.

## Accessibility

- Manrope and JetBrains Mono are self-hosted; no third-party font request.
- All key text pairs pass WCAG AA; small metadata uses the darker muted token.
- Visible 2px focus rings; blue on light surfaces, paper on dark surfaces.
- 44px hero actions and install cards; 32px copy buttons on mobile, 28px on desktop.
- Native buttons, labels on the search and picker, `aria-current` on the active install nav, and a `role="status"` live region for copy results.
- The skill table, install rows, and picker options are rendered at build time, so the five skills and commands remain readable without JavaScript.
- The install page’s FAQ uses a definition list; the steps are ordered lists.

## The install.md flow

The hero card makes one promise: copy the link, give it to your agent, and the agent handles the install. `docs/install.md` is a self-contained prompt, not a shell script. It:

1. detects installed agents with commands, config paths, and the skills CLI’s safe `--list` mode,
2. shows what it found and asks which agents should receive the skills,
3. waits for confirmation,
4. installs the Claude Code plugin or the skills CLI into the confirmed agents,
5. verifies and reports exactly what ran.

The site never claims to know the visitor’s agents. The agent does the detection; the site only provides the link and the manual fallback.

## Content rules

- Commands are exact and copyable. Never shorten `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -y`.
- The install link is `https://mamounhisham1.github.io/vstack/install.md`.
- Do not invent agents, benchmarks, customers, or proof. The agent list comes from the skills CLI.
- “Skills that ship” is the voice anchor. Direct, technical, understated.
- The agent must ask before installing into an unconfirmed agent.

## Files

- `docs/index.html` — homepage; generated table rows and picker options between markers.
- `docs/install.html` — install guide; generated picker and per-skill rows between markers.
- `docs/install.md` — the agent prompt copied from the hero.
- `docs/assets/css/{fonts,base,site}.css`.
- `docs/assets/js/app.js` — copy, filter, picker, `/` shortcut.
- `docs/assets/fonts/` — Manrope and JetBrains Mono subsets plus OFL licenses.
- `scripts/build-skills-json.mjs` — reads `skills/*/SKILL.md`, writes `docs/data/skills.json`, injects rows and pickers.
- `docs/favicon.svg`.

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Stack

Static HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript deployed to GitHub Pages. No frontend build step; `scripts/build-skills-json.mjs` regenerates the skill data and the static skill rows.

## Users

Developers who work with coding agents, primarily Claude Code and OpenCode users arriving from GitHub, skills.sh, or shared links. Secondary audiences: the author, using the site as a living reference, and people evaluating the author's craft. Visitors are usually in a terminal-adjacent context, deciding whether a skill is worth installing. Many now prefer to hand an install link to their agent rather than run commands themselves.

## Product Purpose

vstack is a personal collection of agent skills distributed as one Claude Code plugin or installed individually through the `skills` CLI. The site exists to make the collection legible and to get a visitor to install the set. The primary path is one `install.md` link given to an AI agent; the manual plugin and per-skill commands remain for people who prefer the terminal. Success is a completed install, not time on page.

## Positioning

Every skill starts with `v-`, ships as one readable `SKILL.md`, and has a matching slash command. They are built for shipping real work: `v-build` decomposes features across parallel subagents and lands reviewed PRs; `v-fill-me` reconstructs what happened across branches and worktrees; `v-humanize`, `v-copy-me`, and `v-skill-creator` close the loop from output to workflow to new skill. No hidden runtime, no proprietary service, MIT licensed.

## Operating Context

Visitors read the site beside a terminal, often after seeing a repo or a skills.sh listing. The fastest path is to copy the install link and paste it into Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, or another coding agent. The agent reads the prompt, detects installed agents, asks which should receive the skills, then installs. Manual commands must stay exact, copyable, and visible for visitors who want to run them by hand.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Five skills: `v-build`, `v-copy-me`, `v-fill-me`, `v-humanize`, `v-skill-creator`.
- One Claude Code plugin (`vstack`) installs all five; per-skill installs go through `npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill <id> -y`.
- OpenCode slash commands ship in `.opencode/commands/` as `/<skill-id>`.
- `docs/install.md` is a self-contained agent prompt: detect installed agents, ask which should receive the skills, install all five, verify. The copied link is `https://mamounhisham1.github.io/vstack/install.md`.
- Static site only. Must work on GitHub Pages, without a server, and keep the five skills and commands readable without JavaScript.
- `scripts/build-skills-json.mjs` regenerates `docs/data/skills.json` and injects the static skill rows, install rows, and pickers.
- MIT licensed.

## Brand Commitments

The name is `vstack`. The existing tagline "skills that ship" is a confirmed voice anchor. Tone is direct, technical, and understated; no hype, no invented proof. The `v-` prefix is part of the identity.

## Evidence on Hand

Real skill descriptions in `docs/data/skills.json` and `skills/*/SKILL.md`; real install commands in `README.md`, `.claude-plugin/`, and the skills CLI help; real repository at github.com/MamounHisham1/vstack. There are no testimonials, customer logos, usage metrics, or benchmarks. Do not fabricate any.

## Product Principles

1. Show the command, not a claim about the command.
2. The smallest useful surface: five skills, one plugin, no filler.
3. Every skill is readable source; trust comes from inspection.
4. Ship through real workflow: parallel slices, reviewed PRs, merged results.
5. The agent asks before it installs. Never install into an unconfirmed agent.
6. Understate. Let the work carry the pitch.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Core content must remain readable without JavaScript. Keyboard access, visible focus, reduced-motion support, 44px primary controls, and WCAG AA contrast are required.

# Security Policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report security issues via **GitHub private vulnerability reporting** on `MamounHisham1/vstack` (Security tab → Report a vulnerability).

- Describe: what is affected (skill ID or file path), impact, and reproduction steps.
- Do not include exploits, tokens, or personal data in the report.
- Expect triage as a private advisory; reporters will be credited on request. Do not open public Issues for vulnerabilities.

## Ground rules

- **No secrets in skills.** Skill files (`skills/*/SKILL.md`), commands (`.opencode/commands/*`), and docs must never contain tokens, API keys, passwords, or private URLs.
- **Sanitization gate:** every skill addition or edit must pass the sanitization check described in `CONTRIBUTING.md` (no personal data, no secrets) before merge.
- Dependency or toolchain vulnerabilities: open a regular issue naming the package and version.

# Install vstack

You are an AI coding agent. The user gave you this file so you can install **vstack** for them.

**vstack** is a collection of five agent skills:

- `v-build` — build features end-to-end with parallel subagents
- `v-copy-me` — capture a working session as a reusable skill
- `v-fill-me` — catch up on uncommitted, unpushed, and recently merged work
- `v-humanize` — rewrite technical output in plain language
- `v-skill-creator` — scaffold, publish, and install a new `v-` skill

Repository: <https://github.com/MamounHisham1/vstack>

## Rules

- Do not install anything until the user confirms which agents should receive the skills.
- Do not install into an agent the user did not name.
- Do not guess which agents the user has. Detect them, show what you found, and ask.
- If a command fails, report the exact error and stop. Do not retry with destructive flags.
- Do not modify project files other than what the installers themselves change.

## 1. Detect the agents

Find the AI coding agents installed or configured on this machine. Use the tools that are already present; do not install a new agent just to detect it.

Useful checks:

| Agent | Look for |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude --version`, `~/.claude/` |
| OpenCode | `opencode --version`, `~/.config/opencode/` |
| Codex | `codex --version`, `~/.codex/` |
| Cursor | `cursor --version`, `~/.cursor/` |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini --version`, `~/.gemini/` |
| Cline | `~/.cline/` |
| Roo Code | `~/.roo/` or the Roo Code extension |
| Windsurf | `~/.windsurf/` or the Windsurf app |
| Amp | `amp --version`, `~/.config/amp/` |
| Aider | `aider --version` |
| Goose | `goose --version` |
| Crush | `crush --version` |
| Kilo | `~/.kilo/` |
| Qwen | `qwen --version` |

The `skills` CLI can also detect agents. Run this **safe list command** first; it lists the repository's skills and reports the agent it detects, without installing anything:

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --list
```

If a command is not available, say so. Do not infer an agent from a file name alone.

## 2. Ask before installing

Show the user a short table:

| Agent | Detected? | How you know |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | yes/no | command or path |
| OpenCode | yes/no | command or path |
| Codex | yes/no | command or path |
| Cursor | yes/no | command or path |
| ... | ... | ... |

Then ask exactly one question:

> Which agents should get vstack? Reply with the names, or "all detected".

Wait for the answer. Do not run the installer yet.

If no agents are detected, ask which agents they use and where those agents are installed.

## 3. Install for the confirmed agents

### Claude Code

If the user chose Claude Code, install the plugin. This adds all five skills and keeps them namespaced:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add MamounHisham1/vstack
claude plugin install vstack@vstack
```

In Claude Code the skills are namespaced, for example `/vstack:v-build`.

### Other agents

For every other confirmed agent, install all five skills with the skills CLI. Use the agent IDs the CLI reports. Examples of supported IDs include `opencode`, `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `windsurf`, `cline`, `roo`, `amp`, `aider`, `goose`, `crush`, `kilo`, and `qwen`.

```bash
npx skills add MamounHisham1/vstack --skill '*' --agent <agent-id> [<agent-id>...] --global -y
```

- Use `--global` so the skills are available in every project. If the user explicitly asks for a project-local install, drop `--global`.
- Do not include `claude-code` in this command if you installed the plugin above; that would duplicate the install.
- Do not use `--agent '*'`; install only into the agents the user confirmed.

## 4. Verify

List the global installs:

```bash
npx skills ls -g
```

Filter by an agent if needed:

```bash
npx skills ls -g -a <agent-id>
```

For the Claude Code plugin, confirm the installer reported success, or open `/plugin` in Claude Code and check that `vstack` is installed.

## 5. Report

Tell the user:

- which agents were detected,
- which agents they chose,
- which commands ran,
- what is installed,
- how to use the skills: `/vstack:v-build` in Claude Code, or the skill names in the other agents.

If anything failed, include the exact error and the command that failed.
